Key Activities: Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.
Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Determines changes in the statistical needs of clients; assesses the impact on divisional programs; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) on the results of surveys and studies, survey concepts and methods, and economic / social science theories and principles.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager and Task Force Leader.

Supervises a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for significant multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files/issues; manages the financial resources attached to each statistical program.

1. DECISION MAKING: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information and recommends, for approval, those studies that should be conducted.
Recommends plans to improve and expand the content and direction of existing studies as well as the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the sector.

Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of studies and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Interprets study findings and conclusions and prepares recommendations and advice to senior management on current trends affecting the Sector policies and programs and on the significant factors related to the changing environment.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Manages a unit involved in the conduct of economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of the program. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics and presents rationale on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides expert advice to STC and other professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies on statistical program findings and their application to the area of specialization.

Provides guidance to subordinate staff, other professionals and management on study results, on methods of socio-economic analysis, dissemination, or on statistical techniques and systems; comments on written material to be published by STC.
Negotiates agreements and arranges contracts with consulting firms and suppliers for the acquisition of services.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, compilation, analysis, presentation and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program to recommend changes to management.
Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada to define the objectives and content of studies.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of studies.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on study results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the results on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews statistical techniques, methods and approaches used in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data within a program area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Demography, Health, Justice, Education, Labour, Prices, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). Program areas are often unique in nature and involve different collection, processing, analysis and dissemination activities conducted concurrently.
Analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants and provides senior management with interpretation and recommendations affecting social policy issues.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user needs for statistical information and to translate them into a timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.
